newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Giscard urges Jospin to cut spending.
newsitem.headline: France's Giscard urges Jospin to cut spending.

text.p: Former centrist president Valery Giscard d'Estaing pressed Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on Thursday to make cuts in public spending so France can qualify for a single European currency.

"I came to discuss the problems of economic and monetary union with him and to say how important it was that France be ready for this date," Giscard d'Estaing, who was president from 1974 to 1981, told reporters after an hour-long meeting with Jospin.

They met just before Jospin chaired a government session to finalise a package of tax increases and savings measures to be announced on Monday when an independent audit reveals the true level of the 1997 public deficit, which ministers have said is running at more than 3.5 percent of gross domestic product.
While the new left-wing government seems to be looking largely for extra revenue to plug its budget hole, Giscard d'Estaing said it should concentrate on spending cuts.
"I stressed to him that this approach should mainly be based on reducing spending. We have such a heavy tax burden that, like an exhausted horse, we won't move faster with more whipping," he said.
The former president, who is a member of parliament but no longer holds any leadership role, said deficits were the sole remaining obstacle to launching the euro on time in 1999.
"Naturally, France must join on the right conditions, which means that no one must be able to challenge its entry," he said.
He said he had read the Maastricht treaty text to Jospin, arguing that it meant France should bring its deficit down to close to three percent of GDP this year and reach three percent next year.
There was no comment from the prime minister's office.
